title: Flat linearity of uniform groups
description: Paper (28 pages, PDF and LaTeX source) and the complete code behind its computations. A uniform group is a quotient Z<sub>K</sub><sup>*M</sup> → Γ → Z<sub>K</sub><sup>M</sup> on which S<sub>M</sub> acts by permuting the generators, and a flat representation is a representation π : Γ → U<sub>K</sub> such that each π(g<sub>i</sub>) has the K-th roots of unity as eigenvalues. These are the quasi-flat matrix models of the group duals inside S<sub>KM</sub><sup>+</sup>. We show that Z<sub>K</sub><sup>*M</sup> is flat linear, in the sense that its flat representations separate points, and that for finite groups, flat linearity and stationarity reduce to exact covering problems. We use this to compute a census of the uniform groups in the SmallGroups library of GAP, and to prove results on the Heisenberg and metabelian groups, and on the reflection groups of Raum and Weber.
